purpose: Implements Critical CSS Generation (above-the-fold CSS extraction, inlining, and stylesheet deferral) for the WordPress Performance Optimisation plugin. Adds background generation via Action Scheduler, daily cron regeneration, REST API endpoints, and a UI toggle panel.
riskRationale: Multiple critical bugs make the feature non-functional or crash-producing: the CSS parser fails on minified production stylesheets (producing empty output); inline_ccss() uses theme name instead of template type for hash lookups so generated files are never found; get_page_templates() fatals in Action Scheduler background jobs; suggestion Fix-It navigation for CSS issues is a no-op. These are functional regressions that ship broken code.
breakingChanges: New wp-content/cache/wppo/ccss/ directory for storing generated critical CSS files
Two new REST API endpoints: regenerate_ccss (POST) and ccss_status (GET)
Daily cron hook wppo_ccss_regeneration for CCSS regeneration
New Action Scheduler hook wppo_generate_ccss for background generation per template

text: The PR adds a valuable feature with solid architecture and good integration with existing patterns (Action Scheduler, transients, REST API, cron schedules). The heuristic CSS extraction approach is reasonable for a PHP-only solution. However, the feature contains critical bugs that make it non-functional in real-world scenarios: the CSS parser fails on minified stylesheets (the common case), the inline_ccss() hash computation is wrong so generated files are never found, background jobs can crash, and suggestion navigation for CSS issues is broken.

reasoning: Contains critical bugs that would cause fatal errors in background jobs (get_page_templates outside admin), produce empty critical CSS from minified stylesheets, and render the feature completely inoperative (wrong hash in inline_ccss). The suggestion Fix-It navigation for CSS recommendations is also a no-op. Multiple fixes require significant rewrites (CSS parser, @import resolution) beyond what an automated agent can safely apply.

message: Well-structured single-class file with clean separation of concerns — generation, storage, inlining, deferral, and management. Good naming conventions and consistent use of WordPress coding standards.
Pragmatic heuristic CSS extraction approach for a PHP-only solution. Including @font-face, @keyframes, custom properties, and mobile-first media queries is the right set of primitives.
Smart use of Action Scheduler's as_next_scheduled_action() to prevent duplicate generation jobs, with proper transient-based status tracking.
Clean React component with proper loading states, error handling, and sensible default configurations for each status type.
Good integration with existing plugin architecture — critical CSS hooks are gated behind the setting check and use the same pattern as other features.

get_page_templates() will cause a fatal error when called outside wp-admin context. This function is defined in wp-admin/includes/theme.php which is NOT loaded during Action Scheduler background jobs or non-admin requests, causing the background_generate() method to crash.
suggestion: Wrap get_page_templates() call in a function_exists() guard and skip page templates when the function is unavailable.

message: get_the_time() is used without calling setup_postdata() first. The function relies on global $post being set up correctly. Without setup_postdata($archives[0]), the second parameter is effectively ignored and incorrect values will be returned, producing wrong sample URLs for archive templates.
suggestion: Call setup_postdata() before get_the_time() and wp_reset_postdata() after. Or extract the year/month from the post object directly.

message: The extract_above_fold_css() CSS parser relies on explode("\n", $css) for line-by-line parsing, which has two fatal flaws: (1) minified CSS (single line, common for CDN-served production stylesheets) is treated as one block making selector matching all-or-nothing; (2) multi-line selectors (e.g., "h1, h2,\n h3 {") lose selectors from lines without '{'. In both cases, critical above-fold rules are missed and the output is incomplete or empty.
suggestion: Rewrite the parser to use a token/brace-depth-based approach with preg_match_all() for regular rules (similar to the existing @font-face and @keyframes extraction), accumulating selectors across lines and evaluating complete selector groups against above-fold patterns.

message: inline_ccss() computes the template hash using get_template() (theme folder name, e.g., 'twentytwentyfour') instead of the WordPress page template type (e.g., 'index', 'single', 'page', 'archive'). The resulting hash never matches any CCSS file stored by generate_and_store(), so the <style> tag is never rendered. Background jobs scheduled by inline_ccss() also fail because background_generate() cannot resolve the theme-name hash back to a known template. The entire frontend feature is broken.
suggestion: Add a method that maps WordPress conditional tags (is_front_page(), is_single(), is_page(), is_archive()) to template slugs ('home', 'single', 'page', 'archive'), and use it in inline_ccss() to compute the correct template hash.

message: wp_kses() is the wrong function for sanitizing CSS output inside a <style> tag. wp_kses() is designed for HTML content and strips valid CSS containing '<' (e.g., attribute selectors like [data-value*="<"], or content: "<"). The CSS content is generated by the plugin from the site's own CSS files — no sanitization is needed inside a <style> block since it's not parsed as HTML.
suggestion: Echo the CSS content directly without wp_kses. The content is written by the plugin and read from the plugin's own cache directory.

message: open_ccss_settings is missing from FIX_ACTION_TAB_MAP. The suggestion engine returns this fix action for render-blocking resources and unused CSS suggestions, but the JS map doesn't include it. The Fix-It button's onClick evaluates to null, making the button a no-op for two of the most impactful suggestions.

matches_above_fold() uses strpos() for substring matching of selectors, causing broad false positives: '.container' matches '.container-fluid', '.page-title' matches '.page-title-wrapper', '#nav' matches '#navigation', '*' matches any selector. Additionally, the constant ABOVE_FOLD_SELECTORS includes '*' and '*::before', '*::after' which combined with strpos matching include virtually every rule, bloating critical CSS.
suggestion: Use word boundary or token-based matching instead of strpos(). Split multi-selector CSS rules on ',' and test each individual selector. Remove '*' / '*::before' / '*::after' from ABOVE_FOLD_SELECTORS and include more precise layout primitives instead.

message: External stylesheets are downloaded without resolving @import directives within them. Many WordPress themes use @import in their main style.css to load Google Fonts or other dependencies. These imported rules would be missed, producing incomplete critical CSS. Additionally, @import rules at the top level of extracted CSS are explicitly dropped from output, which means render-blocking dependencies (e.g., font imports affecting visible text) are not inlined.
suggestion: After downloading each stylesheet, recursively scan for @import statements and fetch their contents, resolving relative URLs against the parent stylesheet's base URL. For @import rules encountered during extraction, resolve their URLs, fetch the content, and inline it instead of skipping.

message: Success is logged unconditionally after background_generate() calls generate_and_store(), even if generation failed. generate_and_store() returns bool but the return value is ignored, and Log::add always fires with a success message.
suggestion: Check the return value of generate_and_store() and log accordingly.

message: The SKIP_DEFER_HANDLES array includes 'wppo-critical-css-inline' which does not correspond to any real stylesheet handle. The inline_ccss() method outputs a <style> tag with id="wppo-critical-css", not a wp_enqueue_style handle. This entry is dead code and adds confusion.
suggestion: Remove 'wppo-critical-css-inline' from the SKIP_DEFER_HANDLES array. Inline <style> tags are not processed by the style_loader_tag filter.

message: get_sample_url() is missing a proper PHP return type declaration (string|false). All other methods in the class declare return types.
suggestionCode: private static function get_sample_url( string $template ): string|false {

message: If get_sample_url() returns a password-protected post URL, the generate() method will fetch the password form instead of the actual page content, producing incorrect critical CSS.
suggestion: Consider excluding password-protected posts, or skipping pages that require authentication.

message: generate_and_store() calls Util::init_filesystem() but discards the return value, then checks the global $wp_filesystem which may not have been set. Falls back to file_put_contents, but the pattern is fragile and inconsistent with the existing codebase's filesystem handling patterns.
suggestion: Use the return value of Util::init_filesystem() and pass the filesystem instance explicitly instead of relying on the global.

message: regenerate_all() calls self::clear_all() at the start, deleting all existing CCSS files before queuing background jobs. If some jobs fail, templates are left without any critical CSS.
suggestion: Consider in-place regeneration (overwriting files as they're generated) or regenerating into temporary files and swapping on success.

message: The else branch that calls apiCall('regenerate_ccss') directly is dead code — the component is always rendered by FileOptimization which always passes onRegenerate.
suggestion: Remove the else branch and always require onRegenerate from the parent.

message: The status panel displays raw MD5 hash prefixes (hash.substring(0, 8) + '...') which are not user-friendly. Administrators cannot identify which template a hash corresponds to.
suggestion: Pass template labels alongside hashes from the PHP backend (get_status_all()) and display the template label instead of, or in addition to, the hash.

message: The two new test cases only verify that the Critical CSS switch and panel render. They don't test switch toggling, the regenerate button click, or the integration with onCcssRefresh. This leaves the interactive behavior untested.
suggestion: Add a test that clicks the Critical CSS switch and verifies the panel appears, and a test that clicks the Regenerate All button and verifies apiCall is invoked.
